claims.text: The Pulumi for Terraform Users guide taught how to reference existing Terraform state files from Pulumi, use any Terraform provider in Pulumi programs, import and use Terraform modules directly, convert HCL to Pulumi, and orchestrate Terraform and Pulumi deployments together.
Any Terraform provider can be used in Pulumi programs.
Terraform modules can be imported and used directly in Pulumi.
`new pulumi.StackReference("core-infra")` with `getOutput("vpcId")` is a valid way to reference another stack's outputs (stack name likely needs org/project/stack fully qualified form).
The `terraform.state.S3Reference` class exists in `@pulumi/terraform` (and as `pulumi.terraform.state.S3Reference`) and takes `bucket` and `key` arguments, with a `getOutput` method.
`aws.ecs.Cluster` accepts a `configuration.executeCommandConfiguration` with `kmsKeyId` and `logging: "DEFAULT"` properties.
`pulumi import` can be used to bring Terraform-managed resources under Pulumi management.
State ownership can be transferred gradually from Terraform to Pulumi, resource-by-resource.
The `pulumi import` command syntax `pulumi import aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc main-vpc vpc-12345` (type token, name, ID) is valid, including type tokens `aws:ec2/subnet:Subnet` and `aws:ecs/cluster:Cluster`.
Pulumi policies can enforce infrastructure policies across both Terraform and Pulumi.
`@pulumi/policy` exports `PolicyPack` and `validateResourceOfType`, with policies using `enforcementLevel: "mandatory"` and `validateResource` callbacks taking (resource, args, reportViolation).
`aws.s3.Bucket` has an `acl` property that can be "public-read" or "public-read-write".
The Automation API lets you embed Pulumi in applications for dynamic infrastructure management.
`@pulumi/pulumi/automation` exposes `LocalWorkspace.createOrSelectStack` (with stackName, projectName, program), `stack.setConfig`, and `stack.up({ onOutput })` returning `outputs`.

Component resources can integrate with Terraform behind the scenes, so developers create WebApplications without knowing they depend on Terraform-managed resources, leaving multi-tool complexity to the platform team.
ComponentResource constructor `super(type, name, {}, opts)` and `registerOutputs` are valid component resource API.

`aws.ecs.TaskDefinition` accepts networkMode, requiresCompatibilities, cpu "256", memory "512", and containerDefinitions as a JSON string; `aws.lb.LoadBalancer` accepts loadBalancerType, subnets, internal.
A Pulumi page exists at /docs/intro/concepts/ titled Pulumi Architecture & Concepts.
A page exists at /docs/using-pulumi/adopting-pulumi/ with comprehensive migration strategies.
A page exists at /docs/intro/vs/terraform/ comparing Pulumi and Terraform.
A page exists at /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/.
A page exists at /docs/insights/policy/ covering Policy as Code.
The Pulumi Community page at pulumi.com/community/ offers a community Slack and forum.
The pulumi/examples repository contains hundreds of real-world examples.
The Pulumi YouTube channel is at youtube.com/pulumitv.

Pulumi case studies exist for Snowflake (uses Pulumi with existing tools, multi-cloud strategy), Mercedes-Benz (large-scale infrastructure modernization), and Lemonade (rapid development with Pulumi and Terraform).
Pulumi Support at support.pulumi.com provides professional support for Pulumi Cloud customers.
Contribution links exist: pulumi/pulumi CONTRIBUTING.md on master branch, /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/ page, and pulumi/examples CONTRIBUTING.md.
pulumi.com/events/ lists community events where users can speak; pulumi.com/community/ has user groups.
